notes.title: There's finally a picross game from legendary makers Jupiter on PC
notes.notes: Puzzle nerds, rejoice, for veteran picross makers Jupiter Corporation have finally released a picross game on PC. Logiart Grimoire, released this past week, is a cute little narrative-driven picross game about a magic book that somebody messed up by casting the spells wrong, so now you and weird buddy Emil need to untangle it by solving picross puzzles... notes.title: Release Date Set for the Final Version!
notes.notes:
The release date for the final version of "Logiart Grimoire" on Steam has been decided!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44564844/581e74442d4668d83af9b8b46d48e82e09447b9f.png[/img]


It will be released on March 15, 2024!

Here are the main changes from the Early Access version:

・Addition of the Mysterious Letter 
　・Addition of 115 special puzzles
　・Addition of a special thanks

・Enhancement of various customization features
　・Addition of BGM customization feature
　　・Addition of 5 new BGM tracks
　・Addition of color customization feature for the cursor during puzzles
　・Addition of dark mode for the puzzle UI
　・Addition of ON/OFF function to gray out confirmed hint numbers
　・Addition of ON/OFF function for keyword highlighting in fusion hints
　　(Setting it to OFF increases the difficulty of fusion)
　・Addition of ON/OFF function for post-effect

・Addition of languages
　・French, Spanish, Italian, German, Brazilian Portuguese
　・Traditional Chinese, Simplified Chinese, Korean

・Addition of other features/elements
　・Addition of Emile's accent voice
　・Some changes and additions to Emile's animations
　・Addition of figure viewing function to the collection mode
　・Addition of new achievements

・Other minor feature improvements and bug fixes, etc.

The total number of puzzles is now 419 due to the addition of 115 puzzles in the mysterious letter puzzle. Additionally, three achievements that were not attainable in the Early Access version can now be obtained through updates to the final version.

Furthermore, development for the Nintendo Switch version is underway.
It is scheduled for release in April 2024.
※The content of the game is the same as the Steam version.

We would be delighted if those who have already thoroughly enjoyed the Early Access version would play it again!
So please wait a little longer until the final version is released.

From the Logiart Grimoire Development Team

notes.title: 【A letter from the development team】 Vol.15
notes.notes:
Hello, everyone.
I am 【N】 from the Logiart Grimoire development team!

I will answer the questions we received from our users this time!
Thank you for your questions!

[b][Question]
1.Are there particular themes or subjects that the Jupiter puzzle designers enjoy the most?
2.And can you share any more insight into how the puzzles are made?
3.Are there examples of puzzles that don't work? [/b]

First, I’ll answer your first question!
At Jupiter, there are many puzzle designers, each with their own favorite themes and motifs. The puzzle designer for this project likes the themes and motifs of “food” and “animals”! Especially for “animals”, they are particular about not making the composition from the side or front as much as possible.

Next, I’ll answer your second question!
I can’t explain in detail, but we use a special tool made by Jupiter’s programmers. Using this tool, the puzzle designers tirelessly trial and error to make it work as a puzzle.

Finally, I’ll answer your last question!
There are many puzzles that we can’t make well! However, the puzzle designers use various methods to complete the puzzles with the specified themes and motifs. The size of 5×5 is mostly unable to make a puzzle unless you find a theme that can be expressed in this size, so the most difficult size might be 5×5!

See you again!

notes.notes:
Hello, everyone.
I am 【N】 from the Logiart Grimoire development team!

I will answer the questions we received from our users this time!
Thank you for your questions!

[b][Question]
Are there plans for any Accessibility options?
I would love some Colorblindness filter options, for example. [/b]

First, let me start with the conclusion: in the latest version, we have added an "Color Vision Support" option.

When you enable this feature, all Fusion Hints text will appear in white, and hints represented by cyan text will have a checkmark.
Hints represented by pink text will have an exclamation mark.
The text color for Emil Hints will also be white.

When I received this question, I had an "Aha!" moment (a realization so profound that I even vocalized it with an "Aha!").
I had assumed that there were no elements in this game that required color judgment, as there is no Color Puzzle Mode in this game.

However, when I received this question, I realized that "cyan and pink colors are used in Fusion Hints!" To my embarrassment, I hadn't even considered this until I received this question.
I have reflected on the fact that I need to be more conscious of this to ensure that the game can be enjoyed by a wide range of players.

I immediately shared this with my team members and discussed how we could make the hints easily understandable for users with different perceptions of color.
Due to the fact that perception of colors can vary from person to person, we decided to stop using color for representation.
Instead, we decided to use symbols to represent having (cyan text) and not having (pink text) certain materials.

If you are a user who will utilize the Color Vision Support, I would be delighted if you could provide feedback on usability and other aspects.

I want to express my heartfelt gratitude for making me aware of something so important. Thank you very much!

See you again!

[b][Question]
How did the development of "Logiart Grimoire" start, and what was the inspiration behind it?
Is the fusion element exclusive to this game, or can we expect it in future projects as well?[/b]

I will start by answering the first question!

The trigger for developing "Logiart Grimoire" was the idea of creating a game that would allow players to enjoy playing with pixel art after solving puzzles.
Combining the puzzle-solving part of Logiart with the deduction part using acquired materials would introduce a change in gameplay,
making players increasingly eager to progress through puzzles, which we found to be interesting.
Once the project proposal was approved and the prototype was created successfully, we were fortunate to proceed with the development.

We also decided to introduce a character named Emil to establish a strong sense of the game's world.
We considered it important to incorporate not only 2D elements but also elements of 3D, which we saw as a new challenge.

By incorporating the use of pixel art as a play element, creating a magical world, and introducing elements like Emil,
we aim to develop the game in a way that captures the interest of those who have never played Jupiter's puzzle games before.

Next, regarding the question, "Is the fusion element exclusive to this game?"
At the current stage, I can tell you that we are planning to include the fusion element in the "Logiart Grimoire" series.
We want as many people as possible to enjoy it, and if we have the opportunity to create a sequel,
we are considering enhancing and implementing it further than the current version!

I also plan to provide answers to questions from our users in the next session!
See you again!

notes.title: 【A letter from the development team】 Vol.7
notes.notes:
Hello, everyone.
I am 【N】 from the Logiart Grimoire development team!

Thank you for playing Logiart Grimoire!
We are checking all the comments on the bulletin board and
reviews as a whole development team.
We are very happy to receive so many responses!

We are currently actively working on implementing the
tutorial screen. 
This screen will provide information about Fusion, as taught
by Emil in the early stages, and tips for solving puzzles.

Now, let's discuss puzzle creation.
When Jupiter creates puzzles, we aim to create shapes that
convey the subject matter while using as few lines as possible.
Of course, depending on the subject, we may increase the areas
filled with solid colors rather than relying solely on lines.
(We also use solid colors for areas that need shading, for example.)

However, it's essential to ensure that the puzzle remains solvable.
That's a challenging aspect of our work!
Even if we create shapes that look great, it's a common occurrence
that the puzzle doesn't work as intended.
The puzzle designers are always grappling with this issue.

Furthermore, controlling the difficulty of the puzzles is also quite
challenging.
In particular, making puzzles more difficult is a tough task.
Reducing the filled-in squares tends to increase the difficulty,
but doing so can lead to puzzles that don't work or can't
adequately represent the subject matter.

Conversely, reducing the difficulty of the puzzles is relatively
easier than increasing it.
Adding more filled-in squares allows for some degree of adjustment.

Speaking of "lowering the difficulty," the difficulty level of the
10x10 puzzle "Pickaxe" during the tutorial was significantly lowered
before the early access release.

There was feedback from within the company that it was too
challenging for a tutorial puzzle!

For those of you who have been playing Logiart Grimoire, if you
found any puzzles particularly challenging, please do let us know!
We'd love to hear your feedback.

See you again!

notes.title: 【A letter from the development team】 Vol.3
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44564844/a567b942fe24084b943622ddf472413381925121.png[/img]

This time, we will introduce the puzzle game section of "Logiart Grimoire."

Logiart Grimoire features an assist function to make it easy to play one of the main modes, the puzzle game.

Even if you're new to Logiart puzzles, you can rest assured that you can enjoy them comfortably thanks to the assist function!
Of course, you can also customize the assist function to your liking.

Next, we will introduce the assist features that are included in the game.
Options 1 through 3 can be configured from the options screen,
while options 4 and 5 can be accessed and used from the in-game pause menu during puzzle gameplay.

------------------------------------------------------

[h3]1.Navigation Function[/h3]
This function guides you on how to solve puzzles during gameplay.
There are two types of navigation available.

Blue Number Navigation that informs you of the confirmed rows.
Columns with blue numbers indicate that you can either place a "filled square" or a "×" in them.
This helps you determine which columns to focus on and where you have clues.

Red Number Navigation that informs you of the contradictory rows.
Columns with red numbers indicate that there is a contradiction between "filled squares" and "×."
This helps you identify which columns have contradictions when you're stuck and unable to progress with the puzzle.

[h3]2.Hint Roulette[/h3]
This feature randomly opens up one row or column before starting the puzzle.
It provides you with an initial set of hints, making it particularly suitable for
beginners as the puzzle begins with several hints already available.

[h3]3.Automatic Error Correction[/h3]
This feature automatically corrects incorrect squares when you paint them.
It instantly corrects the squares for you.

[h3]4.Error Check Function[/h3]
This function displays incorrect areas on the board.
It's a useful feature, but you can only use it once until you clear the puzzle.

[h3]5.Rewind Puzzle Function[/h3]
This feature allows you to backtrack up to 100 moves on the puzzle board.
It comes in handy when contradictions arise during the solving process,
as you can easily make corrections and try different approaches.

------------------------------------------------------

If you clear the puzzle without using assist features 1 through 4,
you will achieve a "No Assist Clear," and a star symbol will light up.
For those who excel at puzzles, why not challenge yourself by turning off assist features 1 through 4 and see how you fare?

Additionally, there is a tutorial designed for beginners.
It provides instructions on how to play while you actually solve puzzles,
making it easy for those who are unfamiliar with the puzzle rules to enjoy the game with confidence!

[b]*Please note that other tips and features are not included in the early access release.
 They will be implemented through future updates.[/b]
